::: {.why}
This is the structure that pairs trading actually relies on, and it is the one case where regressing one price on another is not the mistake week 11 warned you about.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Explain cointegration in three sentences to someone who knows regression but not time series.
- Write the error correction representation of a cointegrated pair and say which coefficient is the trade.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Read the Avellaneda and Lee statistical arbitrage paper's model section, where the residual spread is treated as a mean-reverting process. Skip the empirical results; you are after the framing.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Run Engle-Granger by hand rather than by function call: regress one log price on the other, take the residual, and run ADF on it with the correct critical values, which are not the standard ones because the residual came from an estimated relationship. Report both pairs.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Write the error correction form: the change in each price regressed on the lagged residual and on lagged changes. The coefficient on the lagged residual is the speed at which the gap closes and the sign tells you which leg does the adjusting, which is the whole trade in one number.
:::
:::
